assessments.reasoning: The full §10 at [19211,20299) in https://ftp.gnu.org/pub/gnu/Licenses/fdl-1.3.txt ties the proxy’s authority to the Document and permanent election to that proxy’s public acceptance. Its adjacent version-choice alternatives explain how a licensee can have independent permission even when the proxy conditions fail.

limitations: The work’s authorized terms establish the designation and its scope. The GNU license file, its sample Addendum and a catalog tag alone do not establish any particular work’s grant or prove a proxy’s public acceptance.
reasoning: Under §10, a covered Document can authorize a proxy to decide which future versions may be used. When that proxy publicly accepts a version within its authority, licensees gain permanent permission to choose that version for the Document. Election remains optional.
